sections.title: Headline
sections.content: Today’s list is dominated by practical AI-agent infrastructure: skills, coding-agent workflows, model routing, local inference, and multi-agent applications. The strongest single signal is ayghri/i-have-adhd, which added 3,882 stars today, while the broader list also shows strong interest in visual tooling and applied AI.

sections.title: Trending Technologies and Themes
sections.content:
- **Agentic development:** i-have-adhd, superpowers, diagram-design, vercel-labs/skills, and PI-Desktop all focus on making coding agents more usable, capable, or extensible.
- **Local inference and model operations:** llmfit, colibri, and OmniRoute target hardware-aware execution, lightweight local serving, or multi-provider routing.
- **Applied multi-agent systems:** CloddsBot and OpenMAIC apply agents to trading and interactive education rather than only developer workflows.
- **Visual and knowledge tooling:** gods-eye-view, diagram-design, ArmorPaint, awesome-gpt-image-2, and llm_wiki show AI-adjacent demand for visualization, media creation, and persistent knowledge.
- **Languages:** TypeScript leads with 8 of 16 listed repositories; C has 2, JavaScript 2, Python 1, Rust 1, Shell 1, HTML 1, and 1 has no primary language reported.

sections.title: Notable Shifts
sections.content: The notable shift is from standalone model demos toward agent infrastructure and operational tooling: skills distribution, routing across providers, hardware-fit discovery, local-first desktop agents, and domain-specific autonomous systems. The presence of both high-star mature projects such as superpowers and fast-rising newcomers such as i-have-adhd suggests the category is broadening from model experimentation into workflow adoption.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.content: GitHub’s hottest repositories today point to an ecosystem-building phase for AI: developers are packaging agent behavior, routing, evaluation-by-hardware, and domain workflows into reusable tools. Local execution remains important, but the fastest momentum is around making agents reliable and useful inside existing software-development and knowledge-work loops.
